subject: Gilded Health: urgent us-west2 error spike — request for geo-drain & credit approval
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2029-12-04T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: URGENT: Gilded Health — sustained 5xx + p99 spike in us-west2

Team,

Monitoring just alerted: since 07:30 PST we've seen a sustained increase in 5xx (primarily 502/504) for the us-west2 availability zone impacting ~18% of Gilded Health traffic. p99 latency for their production model has jumped from ~420ms -> ~1.6s and their requests/hr dropped ~22% over the last 30m.

What we've confirmed so far:
- Hit pattern: concentrated on us-west2 AZ2 nodes (node pool wz-az2).
- Error pattern: spike in upstream timeouts on the model serving layer, concomitant with K/V cache miss amplification.
- Customer impact: Gilded Health customer ops (ops@gildedhealth.com) reporting elevated error pages and some live users timing out.

Immediate asks:
1) Approve geo-drain (divert Gilded Health to eu-west1) for the next 3 hours while we stabilize. This will incur cross-region egress and potential latency increase for some sessions but will restore success rate.
2) Approve offering a goodwill invoice credit (we suggest 15% of December usage) to reduce customer churn risk — sales + finance sign-off required.
3) Legal/Contracts cc — Gilded has a mid-market contract; we should preemptively inform contracts@gildedhealth.com about the credit.

Attachments: metrics-snapshot-usw2-20291204.png (short graphs), initial-incident-ttl.txt

I recommend we act now and coordinate comms. Waiting will only escalate the SLA exposure.

Hannah
Incident Lead, Regional Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-12-04T08:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Gilded Health — sustained 5xx + p99 spike in us-west2

Thanks Hannah — agree with your recommended approach.

Quick summary / decision request for execs:
- Short-term mitigation: Immediate geo-drain of Gilded Health traffic from us-west2 -> eu-west1. This requires: routing change + warming KV cache + temporarily bumping cross-region throughput for that customer.
- Customer-facing ask: Offer 15% usage credit for December and a follow-up uptime report.
- Risk: Some sessions may see +80–150ms median latency increase; potential data egress costs (~$6k-12k) for the 3-hour window.

Marissa: please confirm you can accept 15% credit and handle customer comms. Rishi: please confirm runbook steps, expected SLO impact, and rollback criteria. If no objections in 10m I will approve the geo-drain and notify operations to execute.

Vivek
VP, Customer Success & Escalations

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-12-04T09:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Gilded Health — sustained 5xx + p99 spike in us-west2

Confirming runbook and risks — see abbreviated plan below (full runbook attached: geo-drain-runbook-v2.pdf).
Action plan (ETA in parentheses):
1) Toggle routing policy for customer GID-654321 to prefer eu-west1 (traffic split 0 -> 100%) (start +2m).
2) Pre-warm KV caches in eu-west1 (parallel) (start immediate; 3–8m).
3) Scale target model pool in eu-west1 by +20% capacity to handle transient burst (apply autoscale override) (5–10m).
4) Monitor success rate, p50/p95/p99, and error budget burn. If success rate > 99.5% and p99 < 900ms then keep drain for 3 hours, otherwise rollback and escalate.

Known risks / mitigations:
- Cross-region session stickiness: we may see token replays for long-running sessions — mitigated by header-based affinity and a short client-side retry window.
- Cost: estimated egress + autoscale delta ~$10k for 3 hours.
- Dependency: third-party DDoS scrubbing in front of customer may also bias 5xx counts; we will correlate logs.

I will kick the runbook now once I get Vivek's go-ahead. Ops will execute; I'll update the thread with step-by-step logs.

—Rishi
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: ops@gildedhealth.com, paul.liu@gildedhealth.com, contracts@gildedhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-12-06T17:02:00-08:00
Subject: Gilded Health — mitigation summary and credit confirmation (us-west2 incident)

Paul / Gilded ops team,

Thank you for your patience while our team worked the incident. Below is an executive summary and next steps: 

What happened: between 07:30–09:50 PST on 2029-12-04 we experienced a regional degradation in us-west2 AZ2 that produced elevated 502/504 responses and p99 latency spikes for your traffic.

What we did: per your permission we temporarily diverted Gilded Health traffic to eu-west1 while we stabilized services in us-west2. The reroute started at 08:45 PST and full traffic returned to us-west2 after successful region remediation at 11:10 PST. During the diversion some long-lived sessions experienced slightly higher latency (median +120ms) but overall success rate improved to 99.7%.

Credit: As discussed, Redwood will apply a 15% usage credit to your December invoice. Contracts will follow up with a credit approval form for signature. 

Follow-up: we will provide a full technical post-mortem and remediation plan by EOD 2029-12-06, and a joint call with your engineering team if helpful.

Attachments included: metrics-snapshot-usw2-20291204.png, geo-drain-runbook-v2.pdf, credit-approval-form.docx

If you'd like us to schedule a 30-min review with our reliability leads, reply with a couple windows and Marissa will coordinate.

Thanks again — we're treating this as a high-priority SLA incident and will be transparent with remediation steps.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success & Escalations
Redwood Inference
